# Technical memory in `docs/`

**Every relevant technical decision, milestone or learning must be recorded as technical memory in the `docs/` of the impacted module.**

Technical memory is how the platform remembers *why* something was done, not just *what* was done. Code lives in git; context, discarded alternatives and consequences live in `docs/` next to the code they govern. Linear is not used — `docs/` and ADRs are the operational record.

## When to create a technical memory

Create one when any of these happens:

- A **phase** or roadmap **block** closes.
- A non-trivial **architectural decision** is applied (provider choice, collection prefixing, deployment model, routing pattern, etc.).
- A **new component** is introduced that other components will start depending on.
- An **environment constraint** is discovered that changes the plan (billing, shared IDs, quota limits, etc.).
- An **irreversible or hard-to-reverse operation** is executed (migration, credential rollover).
- An **incident** worth keeping as future reference is closed.

When in doubt, create it. Better one memory too many than one too few.

## Where to create it

- **Decision of a specific module:** `docs/` of the impacted repo/module (e.g. `biq-methodology/docs/`, `biq-cycle/docs/`).
- **Decision common to the whole app:** `docs/` of the `biq-app` module.
- **Cross-cutting platform/WoW decision:** `basketiq-wow/docs/` (and ADRs in `docs/architecture/adr/` when applicable).

The file is committed with the change that introduces the decision, in the same PR or in the phase-closing PR.

## Format

Markdown file named `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` (or a numbered ADR if the module uses the ADR convention). Minimum content:

- **Context** — what was being solved.
- **Decision** — what was decided.
- **Discarded alternatives** — and why.
- **Consequences** — what changes, what remains as debt.
- **References** — PRs, handoffs, evidence.
